propositions: The tolerant_parse function returns the first parseable JSON object in a model reply, causing schema-valid decoy JSON (tool results, examples, dependency records) to be extracted instead of the intended payload.

Five recurrent instances of incorrect schema objects being extracted have been partially fixed in isolation (commits 9007f290, 5ed760a1, 1aa90fa5) but regress after model provider swaps such as the Bedrock cutover.

The extraction defect class is eliminated via three coordinated thrusts: hardening the prompted path with schema filtering and last-valid-wins selection, enabling provider-native structured output where measured safe, and establishing a reusable measurement harness.
A sentinel output channel with atomic directive-and-extraction co-delivery prevents quoted schema-valid JSON from winning during extraction in prompted paths.
Provider-native structured output is gated on measured thinking-compatibility per model rather than blanket-applied, with unmeasured cells remaining on the hardened prompted path.
Each acceptance criterion is independently deliverable and measured via artifact evidence (corpus tests, config-effect contrasts, before/after raw-output distributions).
